question: A teacher wants students to be able to check the claims in a Claude-drafted study guide for themselves. What should she build into the guide?
options: A) A confidence rating beside each claim showing how certain Claude was when it wrote it.
B) A note at the front explaining that parts of the guide were drafted with Claude's help.
C) Each claim paired with the specific source and page on which a student can find it.
D) A list at the back of every source that was consulted while the guide was being written.
correct_answers: C) Each claim paired with the specific source and page on which a student can find it.
explanations: Incorrect. A self-reported confidence score is not something a student can check against anything.
Incorrect. Disclosure is honest and worth doing, but it gives a student no way to check any particular statement.
Correct. Claim-level sourcing is what makes verification possible for a reader, because it tells them exactly where to look for each statement.
Incorrect. A bibliography shows what was read overall but leaves students unable to tell which source supports which claim.
